newsitem.title: USA: Protein Design reports positive drug trials.
newsitem.headline: Protein Design reports positive drug trials.

text.p: Hoffmann-La Roche Inc and Protein Design Labs Inc said on Wednesday that they had seen positive results from clinical trials on a Zenapax, CellCept drug combination for kidney transplant patients.

"The four-drug regimen (used in the trial) including Zenapax and CellCept appears to achieve a very low incidence of rejection episodes that has not previously been obtained with other drugs and has an excellent safety profile," said Dr. Robert Kirkman, chief of the division of transplantation at Brigham and Women's Hospital in Boston.
Dr. Kirkman presented the data at the annual scientific meeting of the American Society of Transplant Physicians in Chicago and was one of the investigators of the trial.

"We anticipate that Zenapax and CellCept together will become an important part of the standard regimen for the prevention of transplant rejection," said Franz Humer, chief operating officer at Hoffmann-La Roche Ltd.
F. Hoffmann-La Roche Ltd and its New Jersey subsidiary, Hoffmann-La Roche Inc, licensed exclusive worldwide rights to dacliximab, the active ingredient of Zenapax, from Protein Design Labs.
Protein Design Labs Inc develops human and humanized anti-bodies to prevent or treat autoimmune conditions, cancer and viral infections.
If approved by regulatory authorities, Zenapax will be marketed by Roche and PDL will receive royalties based on sales.
